nodes.label: DEC-001: Adopt Agentic Workflow for Repo Development
nodes.author: Luis85
nodes.rationale: Eating our own dog food validates the workflow for real complex software development and makes the repo a reference implementation. The spec-first gate prevents implementation from outrunning design, the most common source of rework in iterative plugin development.
nodes.norm_label: dec-001: adopt agentic workflow for repo development

nodes.label: REQ-0001: Graphify Integration
nodes.author: Luis85
nodes.rationale: The Specorator plugin codebase spans multiple DDD layers, a growing MCP tool surface, and strict port/use-case boundaries hard for AI tools to reason about from raw file reads alone. A persistent knowledge graph lets agents issue targeted graph queries rather than diffuse grep/read sweeps, improving accuracy and reducing context overhead. Committing graphify-out/ gives every contributor instant access without setup.

nodes.label: REQ-0002: Event Tracing Wrapper
nodes.author: Luis85
nodes.rationale: The existing EventBus supports traceId propagation but use cases are called directly from UI composables with no event emission and no correlation ID. Wrapping every interaction in a request/response pair and emitting lifecycle events gives full observability without modifying domain or infrastructure layers. UiContext snapshot enables session replay, support diagnostics, and usage analytics without post-hoc reconstruction.

nodes.label: REQ-0003: Community Plugin Dependency Awareness
nodes.author: Luis85
nodes.rationale: Specorator gains full value composing with the wider Obsidian community-plugin ecosystem. Without an explicit dependency-awareness layer, users with a missing dependency see broken behavior or silent failures. A plugin-agnostic registry plus a narrow domain port keeps domain and application layers decoupled from Obsidian internals per ADR-008, and lets MockBridge and LocalStorageBridge simulate dependency states for unit tests and standalone browser demo.

nodes.label: REQ-0004: Obsidian Native Agent Tool Surface (MCP)
nodes.author: Luis85
nodes.rationale: Specorator's product thesis is that the vault is the agentic operating environment. Honouring the Obsidian Philosophy Contract requires a single, typed, Obsidian-native tool surface. MCP is the stable, versioned contract that lets v1 Claude CLI and v2.0 agentonomous agents share the same tool implementations, accept/reject semantics, and ADR-008 narrow-port boundaries. Without this, future agent integrations regress toward path-string heuristics and unreviewed writes that violate user trust.
nodes.norm_label: req-0004: obsidian native agent tool surface (mcp)

nodes.label: REQ-0005: Dynamic Workflow Execution
nodes.author: Luis85
nodes.rationale: Specorator's value compounds when users can compose reusable agent skills into repeatable, auditable workflows without leaving Obsidian. Canvas is already the native graph surface and SKILL.md is an established markdown contract; combining them lets users assemble pipelines visually and execute them through the same Claude CLI bridge. A vault-backed run directory makes every step inspectable and version-controllable, matching Specorator's spec-first ethos.
